===POST yml===
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Normalize the telephone (strip non-digits, require exactly 10) first: it is the sole
# @RequestBody binding and must run before the DTO's digits-only pattern check would reject
# the raw input. It publishes the normalized body for the validate step.
normalize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  next: normalizeEmail

# Normalize the optional email (validate its format when present, then lower-case it) on the
# already-bound body, before validation and any persistence.
normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  next: normalizeAddress

# Normalize the address (trim/collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand abbreviations) on the
# already-bound body, before validation. Running before validate means an address blank once
# normalized is rejected as a missing required field, and every later address comparison
# (duplicate household, shared household id) sees the normalized form.
normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  next: validate

# Validate so a missing/blank required field is a 400 listing those fields, before any
# entity is built or persisted.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  next: unique

# Reject a telephone already used by another owner (comparing normalized telephones) with a
# 409, before any entity is built or persisted. Reads the same transaction as the writes.
unique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueOwnerTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: uniqueHousehold

# Reject a lastName+address already used by another owner (compared case-insensitively with
# collapsed whitespace) with a 409, unless the request opts in with sharesHousehold=true.
# Runs before any entity is built or persisted, in the same transaction as the writes.
uniqueHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueOwnerHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: cityCapacity

# Reject the request with a 409 when its city already holds the maximum number of owners,
# before any entity is built or persisted. Reads the count in the same transaction as the
# writes so the per-city cap is enforced consistently.
cityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityHasCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

# Record how many existing owners already shared this owner's firstName and lastName
# (case-insensitively) before this create. Reads the count in the same transaction as the
# write, before the new owner is persisted so it is not counted against itself.
assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: defaultRegistrationDate

# Default the registration date to the server's current date when the body supplied none,
# before the owner is persisted. A supplied date is kept.
defaultRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.DefaultOwnerRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

# Assign the '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' customer code, where NNNN is one more than the number
# of owners already in this owner's city. Reads the count in the same transaction as the write
# so the per-city sequence is consistent.
assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
===EnsureCityHasCapacity===
package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner;

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.repository.OwnerRepository;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto.OwnerFieldsDto;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.CityAtCapacityException;

/**
 * Runs in {@code POST /api/owners} after the uniqueness checks, reading the already-validated
 * body as a variable. Rejects the request when its city (compared case-insensitively) already
 * holds {@link #CITY_CAPACITY} or more owners, throwing {@link CityAtCapacityException} for a
 * 409 before any entity is built or persisted. Reads the count in the same transaction as the
 * writes.
 */
public class EnsureCityHasCapacity {

    /** Maximum number of owners a single city may hold. */
    static final int CITY_CAPACITY = 50;

    public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerRepository ownerRepository)
            throws CityAtCapacityException {

        long cityCount = ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
                .filter(existing -> request.getCity().equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getCity()))
                .count();
        if (cityCount >= CITY_CAPACITY) {
            throw new CityAtCapacityException(request.getCity());
        }
    }
}
===CityAtCapacityException===
package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation;

/**
 * Thrown by the create-owner pipeline when the request's city already contains the maximum
 * number of owners (the per-city capacity), so no further owner may be registered there.
 * Carries the offending city so {@link CityAtCapacityExceptionHandler} can report it. Handled
 * as 409 Conflict.
 */
public class CityAtCapacityException extends Exception {

    private final String city;

    public CityAtCapacityException(String city) {
        super("City already at owner capacity: " + city);
        this.city = city;
    }

    public String getCity() {
        return this.city;
    }
}

import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.repository.OwnerRepository;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto.OwnerFieldsDto;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.CityAtCapacityException;

/**
 * Runs in {@code POST /api/owners} after the uniqueness checks, reading the already-validated
 * body as a variable. Rejects the request when its city (compared case-insensitively) already
 * holds {@link #CITY_CAPACITY} or more owners, throwing {@link CityAtCapacityException} for a
 * 409 before any entity is built or persisted. Reads the count in the same transaction as the
 * writes.
 */
public class EnsureCityHasCapacity {

    /** Maximum number of owners a single city may hold. */
    static final int CITY_CAPACITY = 50;

    public void service(@Val OwnerFieldsDto request, OwnerRepository ownerRepository)
            throws CityAtCapacityException {

        long cityCount = ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
                .filter(existing -> request.getCity().equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getCity()))
                .count();
        if (cityCount >= CITY_CAPACITY) {
            throw new CityAtCapacityException(request.getCity());
        }
    }
}

package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation;

/**
 * Thrown by the create-owner pipeline when the request's city already contains the maximum
 * number of owners (the per-city capacity), so no further owner may be registered there.
 * Carries the offending city so {@link CityAtCapacityExceptionHandler} can report it. Handled
 * as 409 Conflict.
 */
public class CityAtCapacityException extends Exception {

    private final String city;

    public CityAtCapacityException(String city) {
        super("City already at owner capacity: " + city);
        this.city = city;
    }

    public String getCity() {
        return this.city;
    }
}

The full suite (the sole `AcceptanceTest`) is green. The change is complete.

## Summary

I implemented the daily owner-registration limit (reject with 429 once 100+ owners have been created today, by `registrationDate`), following the existing per-city capacity feature as the template so the logic lives where it belongs:

- **`EnsureDailyOwnerCapacity`** (function) — counts owners whose `registrationDate` equals the server's current date and throws `DailyOwnerLimitException` when the count reaches the `DAILY_LIMIT` (100). It reads the count within the write transaction, mirroring `EnsureCityHasCapacity`.
- **`DailyOwnerLimitException`** (checked escalation) — carries the offending day.
- **`DailyOwnerLimitExceptionHandler`** — responds `429 Too Many Requests` with a `ProblemDetail`, reusing the shared `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper.
- **`...DailyOwnerLimitException.yml`** — wires the exception to its handler.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted a `dailyCapacity` step after the city-capacity check and before `build`, under `govern: [ transaction ]`, so the cap is checked before any entity is built or persisted.

Each piece is a small single-responsibility unit, and shared logic (problem-detail construction) is reused rather than copied.
